title: Cryogenic STEM-EELS: Connecting Atomic Structure and Excitonic Properties in Twisted 2D MoTe2
content: Moiré engineering in twisted two-dimensional (2D) materials heterostructures has opened new pathways for exploring emergent electronic, excitonic, and topological phenomena. The latest breakthrough includes the observation of integer and fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect in twisted molybdenum ditelluride bilayer (tMoTe2) [1,2]. These physical phenomena are highly sensitive to the atomic structure of the moiré lattice, where interlayer coupling, stacking order, and strain-driven lattice reconstruction play important roles. Understanding the fundamental mechanisms behind these emergent phenomena require atomic-scale structural and spectroscopic characterization with high spatial and energy resolutions.
